name: Drone roof inspection service
one_liner: Use an off-the-shelf drone to photograph roofs for roofers, insurers, landlords and property owners, and sell the inspection reports.
customer: Roofing contractors, insurance adjusters, landlords/property managers, homeowners after storms
offer: Drone roof inspection: 50-60 photos plus a condition report
how_it_makes_money: A fee per inspection. The case study earns $15k-$30k per storm event, and the claimed headline was '$1.5K in 30 minutes'
startup_cost: low-medium (consumer drone from Amazon; in the UK add a CAA Operator/Flyer ID, insurance and possibly an A2 CofC/GVC)
time_to_first_revenue: weeks (start with a couple of jobs a month as a side hustle)
evidence: 'He is doing seven figures a year inspecting roofs' - fwSkDwv2qlU
'Every time there's a storm, he makes 15 to $30,000 in inspections... 15 minutes per inspection' - fwSkDwv2qlU
Drone rooftop inspections are a ~$350M slice of a $23B inspection market growing ~15%/yr - fwSkDwv2qlU
risks: UK storm/insurance-claim dynamics are weaker than in the US

name: Niche long-tail directory websites
one_liner: Build SEO directory sites for searches with low competition and high intent (e.g. 'bee removal near me'), where the current results are outdated or broken.
customer: Local service providers (paid listings and leads), affiliates and advertisers
offer: Featured/paid placements, lead-gen forms, ad and affiliate inventory on a niche directory
how_it_makes_money: Display ads, affiliate clicks, paid featured listings, and selling leads to providers
startup_cost: low (domain, hosting, Ahrefs or a similar SEO tool, AI-generated listings)
time_to_first_revenue: unknown; likely 2-6 months for SEO to rank
evidence: The example niche has 44,000 US searches/month, and the competing directories 'look like from the late 90s' - g5Vd0-y3rG8
'directory websites can make money like a vending machine... ad revenue, affiliate clicks, paid placement, lead gen' - g5Vd0-y3rG8
No revenue figures are given (weak evidence on earnings)
risks: Thin AI content may be penalised
Monetisation is slow until traffic arrives
UK/PT search volumes are much smaller than US

name: Bulk book pallet arbitrage + live selling
one_liner: Get book pallets or bulk lots for free or very cheap, then resell individual books online and through live-selling apps, using AI to handle the listings.
customer: Online book buyers and live-shopping audiences (Whatnot, eBay, Vinted-style platforms)
offer: Used/collectible books, single or in bundles
how_it_makes_money: Retail margin on each unit; pallets bought for $1 grossed $5,000, and $6 items sell for $40 on Whatnot
startup_cost: low (~$1 pallets or free books; needs storage and transport)
evidence: 'She buys $1 pallets and sells them for $5,000' with about 3 hrs/week - kHRKeDqsoG8
Works out to ~$75/hr ('that's $150,000 a year' full-time) - kHRKeDqsoG8
'I snap the pictures, and then AI literally does everything else' - kHRKeDqsoG8
risks: Finding cheap pallets in the UK is uncertain
Live selling needs showing up on camera at set times

name: Google/YouTube Ads agency for high-LTV home services
one_liner: Run Google Search and YouTube ad campaigns for local home-service businesses (HVAC, roofing, cleaning) that aren't marketers themselves.
customer: Local home-service businesses where a customer's lifetime value is in the thousands
offer: Managed Google/YouTube ad campaigns plus a landing-page fix ('answer 3 questions in 3-5 seconds')
how_it_makes_money: A monthly retainer or a percentage of ad spend, with optional pay-per-lead
startup_cost: low (skills plus software; client pays the ad spend)
time_to_first_revenue: weeks once a first client signs
evidence: A client asked to pause ads, and the reply was 'Can you stop printing money, please?' - mIxocaCBgwY
'Any type of home service business where... lifetime value of a client is in the thousands is a great way to go' - mIxocaCBgwY
'If you know these things, that gives you the edge over 90% of your competitors' - mIxocaCBgwY
risks: Ad costs are competitive in some niches
No agency revenue figures are stated

name: Short-form to newsletter audience funnel
one_liner: Post face-to-camera short videos that drive followers to a niche newsletter, then make money from the newsletter through sponsors or your own offers.
customer: Sponsors/advertisers and newsletter readers buying products
offer: A niche newsletter with sponsorship slots and your own products
how_it_makes_money: Newsletter sponsorships, affiliate links, and launching your own products to the list
evidence: Went from 50 to 45,000 followers overnight from one phone video, which he values at '$40,000 worth of value' - fogwK_iU7Zc
Subscribers open ~55% of emails with a 4% CTR, and roughly 1 subscriber comes per 5,000 views - fogwK_iU7Zc
Weak on direct revenue: no newsletter revenue figure is stated
risks: Results are lottery-like and depend on going viral
Conversion from short-form to email is low
Slow path to cash; works best as a distribution layer for other businesses
